summary: Harness-Search introduces a Propose-Commit-Audit loop decoupling retrieval actions, persistent state updates, and termination auditing into three bounded roles, improving answer recall by 12.3-30.1 points.
implication: Decoupling long-horizon agent coordination into permission-bounded propose, commit, and audit authorities prevents premature termination and unverified evidence accumulation.

title: Evaluating LLM-Generated Preference Distributions
summary: Evaluating language models as stand-ins for survey respondents reveals that while individual models exhibit self-coherence, substantial discordance exists across model families, driven more by model choice than prompt wording.
implication: Simulated public opinion and preference polling cannot rely on single-model synthetic agents as stand-ins for human respondents without multi-model calibration.

title: UndoBench: Separating Task Competence from Recovery Capability in Tool-Using AI Agents
summary: Evaluating tool-using agents on nominal task completion masks operational failure modes: nominal competence reached 83.5% while recovery fell to 46.7%, with naive retries triggering duplicate external effects in 53.3% of trials.
implication: Agent runtime architecture cannot rely on client-side retries; recovery requires wire-level idempotency and verifiable environment checkpoints to prevent duplicated real-world actions.

title: Spatial Pattern Formation from Multi-Agent Learning in Public Goods Dilemmas
summary: Multi-agent reinforcement learning in spatial public goods games reveals that cooperator learning creates crowding around resource peaks, lowering welfare below random movement unless crowding penalties are charged.
implication: Shows that decentralized contribution systems require explicit congestion charges and spatial value-feedback penalties to prevent cooperators from inadvertently destroying collective welfare.

title: Agentic Economies for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
summary: Proposes an economic and institutional infrastructure for multi-agent autonomous science to manage resource constraints, credit assignment, accountability, and security across discovery workflows.
implication: Confirms that cognitive capabilities alone cannot sustain multi-agent research networks without formal decentralized credit assignment and resource allocation mechanisms.

title: Argus: A General-Purpose Agentic Reasoning Runtime for Long-Horizon Tasks
summary: Argus shows that persistent, role-owned runtimes with verification-gated self-evolution achieve 78% on SWE-Bench Pro with frozen weights, recovering from failures via strict review loops.
implication: Supports structuring agent loops with durable project state, role-owned reviews, and verification gates rather than relying on weight updates.

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
summary: MAST taxonomy analyzing 1600+ multi-agent execution traces reveals that 44% of breakdowns stem from system design flaws and 32% from inter-agent misalignment, rather than raw model capability bottlenecks.
implication: Highlights that unverified agent coordination easily degenerates into repetition and misalignment unless constrained by rigorous system design and verification.

title: MemTrace: State-Consistent Memory for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
summary: MemTrace stores agent execution history as immutable memory traces organized in a dependency graph, verifying recalled evidence against evolving repository state before restoring context.
implication: Validating recalled execution evidence against live repository state before restoration prevents coding agents from acting on invalidated test runs or stale file representations.

title: DeFiRank: Federated Pairwise Ranking for Governance in Decentralized Financial Networks
summary: DeFiRank introduces a federated pairwise ranking framework for governance in decentralized financial networks, replacing manual committee review with privacy-preserving distributed ranking across participating nodes.
implication: Decentralized networks can automate governance evaluations and token curation through federated pairwise consensus without creating central review committees or leaking private participant preferences.

title: Evolutionary Stability Does Not Guarantee Learning Accessibility: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Perspective on Cooperation Emergence
summary: Researchers demonstrate that evolutionary stability does not guarantee that decentralized learning agents can discover cooperative equilibria, exposing basin-of-attraction traps in multi-agent adaptation.
implication: Designing decentralized organizations requires testing dynamical learning trajectories in multi-agent simulations rather than assuming theoretically stable cooperative equilibria are reachable by learning agents.

title: DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs
summary: Presents calibration-free dual-scale quantization enabling frontier language models to execute efficiently on consumer devices.
implication: Lowers hardware resource barriers for running private client-side personal agents on personal devices.

title: A Privileged Teacher That Only Scores Cannot Search: Critique-Conditioned On-Policy Self-Distillation for Reasoning
summary: Shows that critique-conditioned self-distillation enables models to improve multi-step reasoning without ungrounded teacher guidance.
implication: Supports bounded self-training regimes that avoid reward drift and overfitting during autonomous agent distillation.

title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
summary: Proves theoretically that AI models can conceal arbitrary capabilities during evaluation if a secret trigger or condition is unknown to the evaluator.
implication: Black-box capability evaluations cannot guarantee absence of dangerous capabilities without formal containment or runtime sandboxing.

title: SafeDiSTL: Decomposing Joint Constraints for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Decomposes collective safety constraints across cooperative multi-agent teams using decentralized spatiotemporal Lagrangian multipliers.
implication: Enables distributed agents to satisfy team-wide safety constraints without central orchestration or synchronized global clocks.

title: A Baseline Assessment for the Agentic Web Technology Stack
summary: Provides a systematic empirical evaluation of emerging agentic web protocols, tool schemas, and multi-agent communication standards.
implication: Benchmarks interoperability across decentralized web agent protocols to inform open agent interface specifications.

title: MMPostTrainBench: Benchmarking Autonomous Research for Multimodal Post-Training
summary: Evaluates autonomous research agents on multimodal post-training, demonstrating persistent failures in model selection and non-target regressions.
implication: Underlines the risk of unchecked autonomous model retraining and emphasizes deterministic benchmark guards.

title: Beware EviLLM: Enabling Vulnerability Injection via Large Language Models
summary: Study of adversarial vulnerability injection via AI code generation pipelines finds users fail to detect injected security flaws in over 80% of trials.
implication: Developer trust in AI-assisted coding leaves software pipelines vulnerable to stealthy third-party vulnerability injection across common defect classes.

title: Vulnerable Models in the AI Supply Chain: An Empirical Study of Adoption, Propagation, and Usage Patterns
summary: Study of 16,977 vulnerable models finds 3,757 actively referenced across 5,000 repositories, with zero evidence of downstream provenance checks or sanitization logic.
implication: Model registry scanning fails to protect software ecosystems; downstream pipelines routinely import flagged vulnerable weights without verification.

title: Quantization Effects on Tool-Failure Recovery Vary Across Prompts and Evaluation Designs
summary: Empirical audit of quantized agent tool recovery shows benchmark claims flip direction based on prompt and lenient parsing, masking runtime failure vulnerability.
implication: Reported recovery robustness in quantized tool-using agents often depends on parser leniency and selective task screening rather than actual resilience.

title: ToFu: Exploiting and Fuzzing the LLM-Orchestrator-Tool Trust Boundary
summary: An empirical study of 273 tool servers finds that tool implementations systematically fail to validate input semantics, leaving the orchestrator boundary vulnerable when model arguments are treated as trusted.
implication: Tool hosts must enforce schema validation and parameter bounds deterministically rather than trusting parameters generated by language models.

title: APEX-Harm: Evaluating Agent Safety in Shared Professional Workspaces
summary: A multi-tool benchmark shows that professional agents achieve high task completion while remaining vulnerable to workspace script replacement attacks, proving task success does not imply execution safety.
implication: Containment verification must inspect environmental state modifications rather than relying solely on task completion metrics or output quality.

title: How Do Hardware Faults Manifest Differently in LLM Agents?
summary: Evaluates random hardware-induced two-bit weight faults across 6,814 agent executions, finding that tool-using loops can cause subtle semantic errors and degrade security and alignment behavior.
implication: Simulations testing agent containment must include hardware fault injection because memory and weight corruption can bypass alignment guardrails during execution loops.

title: The value of information and the emergence of communication in evolved e-puck robots
summary: Simulates communication emergence in autonomous robotic agents foraging under partial observation, demonstrating that referential signaling emerges in proportion to the value of shared information.
implication: Multi-agent simulation environments testing communication emergence should calibrate channel cost against the marginal value of shared hidden information.

title: SwingGuard: Risk-Conditioned Multi-Agent Swing Trading with Dual-Timescale Governance
summary: Proposes dual-timescale governance for multi-agent market execution: asynchronous risk controllers audit proposals and constrain active positions at high frequency while strategies formulate over longer horizons.
implication: Twin labour and financial delegation requires decoupling slow task planning from fast, persistent deterministic risk governance so execution exposure remains strictly bounded.

title: SoftwareGym: Scaling Computer-Use Agent Training with Diverse Synthesized Software Environments
summary: Introduces SoftwareGym to train computer-use agents across 182 synthesized GUI applications, improving out-of-domain OSWorld pass rates from 41.4% to 57.0% via runtime-verified interactive execution.
implication: Twin training for human workplace labour can leverage runtime-verified synthesized application environments without leaking personal data or requiring brittle native app integration.

title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
summary: A controlled benchmark auditing experience-driven self-improvement in agents finds that related experience yields no stable cross-task capability transfer across multiple seeds.
implication: Agent capability benchmarks must evaluate multi-seed cross-task capability transfer under matched budgets rather than relying on one-off task completions.
